# **Architectural Analysis of BandaGo POS: Core ERP Engine, Data Layer Implementation, and External Integration Endpoints**

## **Executive Disambiguation and Platform Overview**

A technical investigation into "BandaGo POS" requires immediate disambiguation between two distinct commercial entities operating under identical nomenclature across different industries. In the United States transportation sector, **Bandago Van Rental** (legally operating as Digby Adler Group, LLC dba Bandago, LLC, founded in 2003 by Sharky Laguana) is a nationwide passenger van rental company catering to touring musicians1. That entity appears in Point-of-Sale (POS) literature exclusively as a merchant adopter, having integrated Solana Pay for blockchain-based physical commerce and DataX's RentalOS for fleet booking and customer ledger management1.  
Conversely, the dedicated software platform known as **BandaGo** is an enterprise-grade, cloud-based outpatient Health Management Information System (HMIS), pharmacy inventory controller, and Point-of-Sale (POS) platform engineered by **Banda Health**6. Headquartered in Colorado Springs, Colorado as a registered 501(c)(3) public charity (EIN: 81-3695611) with its primary software engineering and clinical implementation hub in Nairobi, Kenya, Banda Health designed BandaGo specifically for low-resource healthcare facilities and storefront pharmacies across emerging markets7. As of August 2025, BandaGo operates in production across more than 140 clinics in four countries, managing clinical workflows, medicine supply chains, and POS cash flows for over 900,000 patients annually7.

| Platform Dimension | Technical and Operational Specification |
| :---- | :---- |
| **Platform Name & Provider** | BandaGo by Banda Health (formerly OpenHMIS)6 |
| **Target Facility Accreditation** | Kenya Digital Health Agency (DHA) Certified for Level 2 (Dispensaries) and Level 3A (Health Centers & Outpatient Clinics)13 |
| **Clinical & Operational Scope** | Strictly optimized for Outpatient Operations, Pharmacy POS, Lab Diagnostics, and Maternal & Child Health (MCH); Inpatient features excluded6 |
| **Core Backend Stack** | Java, iDempiere Open Source ERP/CRM/SCM/POS, OSGi Plugins (base, graphql), JasperReports7 |
| **Database & Procedural Layer** | PostgreSQL with custom PL/pgSQL stored functions and automated SQL/2-Pack migrations10 |
| **Frontend & API Layer** | ReactJS and TypeScript Single-Page Application (SPA) communicating via a custom GraphQL API10 |
| **Commercial & SLA Profile** | KES 5,500/year or KES 500/month (USD 50/year outside Kenya) via M-Pesa Paybill 600100; 99.9% server-side uptime target6 |

BandaGo's market positioning addresses a structural failure in developing healthcare ecosystems: frontline "clinics without doctors"—typically run by Clinical Officers, Nurses, and pharmacists in informal urban settlements and rural villages—suffer from severe revenue leakage, drug theft, expired pharmaceuticals, and stock-outs that force clinicians to substitute suboptimal treatments7. While competing DHA-certified hospital software vendors charge up to KES 500,000 (approximately USD 3,800) in prohibitive upfront licensing fees alongside heavy maintenance retainers, BandaGo delivers full regulatory compliance, automated demand forecasting, and Health Information Exchange (HIE) connectivity for KES 5,500 per year13. Early clinical deployments demonstrated that BandaGo's automated replenishment algorithms reduced medicine stock-outs to zero and lowered overall inventory carrying and procurement costs by 40% to over 50%8.

## **Evolutionary Trajectory: From OpenMRS Modules to an iDempiere ERP Core**

To understand how BandaGo operates under the hood today, an architect must examine its foundational re-engineering from a medical-records add-on into a standalone Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) engine. Banda Health originated under the name **OpenHMIS**, initially constructing clinical POS and inventory tools as Java .omod extensions running inside the **OpenMRS** (Open Medical Record System) platform7. During this first-generation phase, the stack relied on OpenMRS 1.9.x through 2.1.x, MySQL 5.6/5.7, Hibernate ORM, Spring MVC, BackboneForms (openhmis.backboneforms), Groovy Server Pages (GSP), and Liquibase XML database migrations11. The legacy architecture was divided across four primary repositories: openmrs-module-openhmis.commons (shared data access patterns such as BaseObjectDataServiceImpl), openmrs-module-openhmis.inventory (stockrooms, items, and stock operations), openmrs-module-openhmis.cashier (bill creation, cash points, and shift timesheets), and openmrs-module-openhmis.plm (Persistent List Manager)7.  
![][image1]  
Two structural pressures forced Banda Health to abandon the OpenMRS module paradigm in favor of **iDempiere ERP**7. First, OpenMRS was fundamentally architected as a clinical observation repository (centered on an Entity-Attribute-Value obs table) rather than a double-entry financial ledger or supply chain engine; as noted in OpenMRS architectural discussions, facilities requiring rigorous billing, multi-location inventory valuation, payroll, and tax compliance inevitably outgrow ad-hoc clinical forms and require a true ERP backend13. Second, coupling POS and inventory schemas to OpenMRS core upgrades created severe maintenance fragility. Community deployment logs across OpenMRS 2.5, 2.6, and 2.7 reveal recurring Liquibase schema failures—such as missing primary key constraints on inv\_recipient blocking foreign key creation (inv\_stock\_operation\_recipient\_id\_fk) on inv\_stock\_operation—alongside ClassNotFoundException crashes caused by deprecated Spring DefaultAnnotationHandlerMapping classes and REST conversion errors on org.openmrs.module.openhmis.cashier.api.model.Bill12. By December 2021, Banda Health leadership confirmed that active development had ceased on the legacy OpenMRS Cashier module26.  
To replace the legacy stack, Banda Health forked **iDempiere** (banda-health/idempiere and banda-health/idempiere-docker)—an enterprise OSGi (Equinox) Java ERP/CRM/SCM/POS suite evolved from Compiere and ADempiere—and paired it with **PostgreSQL** and a modern **ReactJS/TypeScript** web frontend7. Rather than modifying iDempiere's core ERP source code, BandaGo encapsulates all clinical, pharmacy, and POS customizations inside a dedicated monorepo of OSGi plugins and database scripts (banda-health/idemp-plugins)14. This architectural pivot inverted the system design: instead of bolting fragile accounting onto a medical record system, BandaGo embeds streamlined outpatient clinical workflows directly inside a battle-tested, double-entry ERP and inventory engine13.

## **Full-Stack Client and Server Architecture**

BandaGo operates as a multi-tenant, cloud-hosted Software-as-a-Service (SaaS) platform engineered for high reliability over constrained East African network connections6. The architecture is strictly decoupled into a modern browser-based client tier, a GraphQL API translation tier, an OSGi business logic tier, and a relational database tier10.  
![][image2]

### **Frontend Client and Low-Touch Operational Design**

While stock iDempiere ships with a server-rendered ZK Ajax desktop interface designed for back-office accountants, BandaGo replaces the user-facing experience with a custom Single-Page Application (SPA) constructed in **ReactJS** and **TypeScript**10. The client application runs inside any standard web browser on a desktop, laptop, or tablet, eliminating local server maintenance at the clinic level while delivering automated summary reports directly to clinic owners' smartphones8.  
The frontend client architecture is purpose-built around frontline outpatient velocity and "low-touch" adoption13. Because target facilities operate in environments with intermittent power stability, high patient-to-clinician ratios, and non-technical medical staff, the UI is segmented into role-specific workspaces: Patient Registration & Live Queue Management, Clinical Consultation & Diagnostics, Laboratory Panel Processing, Pharmacy Inventory & Dispensing, and Cashier POS & Financial Ledgers6. Furthermore, Banda Health actively embeds self-sufficiency mechanisms directly into the client layer—including in-app AI-driven prompts, automated contextual UI feedback, color-coded drug expiration badges, and embedded short-form video tutorials—to eliminate manual onboarding friction and prevent informal staff workarounds13.

### **Backend OSGi Plugin Ecosystem and Build Pipeline**

Under the hood, the backend is powered by Banda Health's customized fork of **iDempiere** running on Java and packaged via Maven Tycho and Docker (banda-health/idempiere, banda-health/idempiere-docker, and banda-health/idemp-plugins)7. iDempiere's modular OSGi architecture allows BandaGo to inject domain-specific healthcare and POS behavior onto existing ERP layers without altering the underlying ERP core14. All proprietary and open-source extensions are consolidated within the banda-health/idemp-plugins repository, which is composed of 88.2% Java, 7.0% PL/pgSQL, 4.4% TypeScript, 0.3% Shell, and 0.1% Python14.

| Repository Module / Directory | Architectural Role in BandaGo Backend |
| :---- | :---- |
| **base (OSGi Plugin)** | Houses all custom BandaGo data models, OSGi model event listeners, server processes, and column callouts14. |
| **graphql & graphql-feature** | Implements the GraphQL schema, resolvers, and HTTP endpoint exposing BandaGo business logic to the ReactJS client14. |
| **migration (DB Layer)** | Contains automated SQL migration scripts, 2-Pack packages, and custom PL/pgSQL stored functions executed against PostgreSQL14. |
| **data / data/import** | Stores CSV and configuration seed files injected into \[IDEMPIERE\_HOME\] to bootstrap new clinic tenants during client creation14. |
| **reports (JasperReports)** | Contains .jrxml report templates compiled into .jasper binaries for POS receipts, shift summaries, and patient transactions14. |
| **base-test & reports-test** | JUnit/OSGi test plugins utilizing chuck-test-framework to validate model events, server processes, and report accuracy in CI/CD14. |
| **graphql-test & external-mocks** | TypeScript/Jest end-to-end integration suite testing GraphQL workflows (e.g., visitReceiptReport.test.ts) and mocking external APIs14. |
| **Observability & CLI Tooling** | Companion TypeScript repositories: idempiere-log-parser (parses GraphQL logs), data-integrity-alerter (flags DB anomalies), and banda-cli7. |

During compilation, executing mvn verify \-Didempiere.home.dir=/path/to/idempiere compiles the base and graphql OSGi bundles, compiles all JasperReports templates, and copies the seed data/import files, DB migration scripts, and compiled reports into their designated runtime directories within the iDempiere installation14. For local engineering and CI parity, a unified wrapper script (./dev.sh) orchestrates Docker containers (dev-docker, docker-compose.dev.yml, docker-compose.deploy.yml), running Eclipse (server.product), executing database migrations (./dev.sh migrate), and running headless SOAP and Jest GraphQL test suites against a pre-seeded PostgreSQL test database14.

## **Data Layer Architecture and Entity Schema Implementation**

Examining BandaGo under the hood requires analyzing how domain entities—people, customers/patients, medicines, clinical visits, and POS transactions—are implemented and reserved within the PostgreSQL data layer10. While direct directory browsing of the raw SQL files inside idemp-plugins/migration and idemp-plugins/graphql is restricted in external crawls29, the exact data layer mechanics can be reconstructed with high architectural certainty because BandaGo is built directly on **iDempiere's Application Dictionary (AD\_\*)** and Banda Health's documented base plugin conventions14.  
In iDempiere, the database schema is metadata-driven. Every table (AD\_Table), column (AD\_Column), field (AD\_Field), validation rule (AD\_Val\_Rule), and reference data type (AD\_Reference) is registered inside the PostgreSQL Application Dictionary. When Banda Health engineers create a new table or reserve custom healthcare columns on an existing ERP table via the ./migration workflow, the base plugin generates corresponding persistence interfaces (I\_\*), generated model classes (X\_\*), and custom domain extension classes (M\*)14.  
Business rules are enforced at the data layer through four core mechanisms explicitly identified in the base plugin documentation14. First, **Custom Models** consist of Java classes extending iDempiere's PO (Persistent Object) class to map PostgreSQL rows to strongly-typed domain objects14. Second, **Model Events (IEventTopics)** act as OSGi event handlers triggered synchronously before or after database transactions (PO\_BEFORE\_NEW, PO\_BEFORE\_CHANGE, DOC\_BEFORE\_COMPLETE, DOC\_AFTER\_COMPLETE) to enforce clinical and financial integrity14. Third, **Callouts (IColumnCallout)** operate as field-level triggers that dynamically calculate or populate dependent fields when an attribute changes14. Fourth, **Processes (SvrProcess) and PL/pgSQL Functions** serve as server-side batch operations and stored PostgreSQL procedures—accounting for 7.0% of the entire idemp-plugins codebase—that execute complex aggregations such as medicine demand calculation, client provisioning, and statutory report generation8.

### **Multi-Tenancy, Security, and People Management**

Every table in BandaGo's PostgreSQL database reserves seven mandatory system columns defined by the iDempiere persistence engine, ensuring row-level multi-tenancy and auditability across all 140+ clinics7. The primary tenant partition key is AD\_Client\_ID (NUMERIC(10,0)), where each subscribed clinic organization is provisioned as an isolated AD\_Client bootstrapped using the CSV and 2-Pack templates in ./data/import, analogous to the GardenWorld base client used in CI testing14. Within a tenant, AD\_Org\_ID (NUMERIC(10,0)) serves as the facility or branch partition key, enabling a single clinic owner to scale operations across multiple physical pharmacy or clinic locations while maintaining separate or consolidated stock and cash ledgers8. Record lifecycle and auditability are governed by IsActive (CHAR(1)), which acts as a soft-delete and retirement flag ('Y' or 'N') so historical clinical and financial records are never physically deleted from the ledger, alongside four audit columns (Created, CreatedBy, Updated, UpdatedBy) that store timestamps and foreign keys referencing AD\_User\_ID for complete user activity tracking6. Finally, every table reserves a \<TableName\>\_UU (VARCHAR(36)) Universally Unique Identifier (UUID) column, which is indexed and heavily utilized by the graphql plugin for stateless external entity referencing14.  
"People" within BandaGo are bifurcated into **System Users / Clinical Staff** and **Employees**, mapped across the following data structures:

| Entity Role | Underlying iDempiere / BandaGo Table | Reserved Fields & Implementation Mechanics |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **Tenant & Branch Context** | AD\_Client, AD\_Org | Reserves AD\_Client\_ID, AD\_Client\_UU, AD\_Org\_ID, and AD\_Org\_UU on every database row to enforce strict multi-tenant clinic and branch isolation8. |
| **Authenticated System Users** | AD\_User | Stores AD\_User\_ID, AD\_User\_UU, Name, EMail, Phone, Password (hashed with salt), IsLocked, and DatePasswordChanged to enforce SLA password complexity and rotation policies6. |
| **Role-Based Access Control (RBAC)** | AD\_Role, AD\_User\_Roles, AD\_Window\_Access, AD\_Process\_Access | Restricts user access to the minimum data essential for job functions (e.g., Admin, Clinician, Lab Tech, Pharmacist/Inventory, Cashier) to prevent drug and cash theft6. |
| **Clinic Staff & Payroll Entities** | C\_BPartner (IsEmployee \= 'Y') | Links staff AD\_User records to Business Partner ledgers (C\_BPartner\_ID) to process staff payroll, track cash advances, and post salary expenses to the General Ledger13. |
| **Clinician & Cashier Shifts** | C\_POS / Custom Shift & Audit Tables | Tracks active cashier logins, cash points, and collections per shift (evolved from the legacy OpenHMIS Timesheet and Shift Summary architecture)13. |

### **Customers, Patients, and Outpatient Clinical Visits**

In BandaGo's unified POS and HMIS data model, a **Patient** and a **POS Customer** are a single unified entity implemented by extending iDempiere's core Business Partner table (C\_BPartner paired with C\_BPartner\_Location and C\_BP\_Group)13. In standard ERP operations, C\_BPartner tracks anyone with whom the facility transacts (IsCustomer \= 'Y' for patients and walk-in pharmacy buyers; IsVendor \= 'Y' for wholesale pharmaceutical suppliers; IsEmployee \= 'Y' for clinic staff)8.  
Through the base plugin and ./migration scripts, BandaGo reserves custom patient-centric columns (conventionally prefixed in iDempiere plugin development, e.g., BH\_\* for Banda Health) directly on C\_BPartner and dedicated clinical visit tables14:

| Domain Concept | Primary Table Mapping | Key Reserved Fields & Data Layer Implementation |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **Patient / Customer Master** | C\_BPartner (IsCustomer \= 'Y') | Standard ERP fields: Value (Patient ID/Chart Number), Name (Full Name), TotalOpenBalance (real-time unpaid patient debt), SOCreditStatus. Custom BandaGo fields: Gender/Sex, Date of Birth / Approximate Age, National ID, SHA/NHIF Member Number, Next of Kin, and Primary Phone (C\_BPartner\_Location / AD\_User) used for automated SMS follow-ups and debt reminders6. |
| **Patient Visit / Encounter** | Custom Visit Model (e.g., BH\_Visit / Extended C\_Order) | Verified by visitReceiptReport.test.ts14. Represents a discrete outpatient encounter linking the patient (C\_BPartner\_ID), Visit Date, Visit Type (Outpatient Consultation, Pharmacy Walk-in, Lab-Only, MCH), Live Queue Stage (Waiting Triage, With Clinician, In Lab, At Pharmacy, At Cashier, Completed), and attending clinician (AD\_User\_ID)6. |
| **Clinical Notes & Vitals** | Custom Clinical Observation Tables (linked to Visit) | Captures chief complaints, triage vitals (temperature, blood pressure, weight, height, BMI), physical exam notes, patient medical history, and automated sick-off sheet metadata6. |
| **ICD-11 & MOH705 Coding** | Custom Diagnosis / Coded Concept Tables | Implements integrated **ICD-11** diagnostic coding mapped to Kenya Ministry of Health **MOH705** (Outpatient Morbidity Summary) age-bracket disease categories (Under 5 years vs. Over 5 years, New vs. Re-attendance visits)8. |
| **Laboratory & MCH Modules** | Custom Lab & Program Tables / Service M\_Product | Reserves customizable lab panel definitions (including microbiology culture & sensitivity results) and structured government Maternal & Child Health (MCH) workflows: Family Planning (live in production), Antenatal Care (ANC), Child Welfare Clinic (CWC), and Immunization6. |

This unified Customer/Patient table design yields a major second-order architectural advantage: whether an individual walks into a storefront pharmacy solely to purchase over-the-counter paracetamol at the POS or undergoes a full clinical consultation with lab panels and SHA insurance billing, the transaction attaches to the exact same C\_BPartner\_ID record8. Clinicians and owners can pull up a patient's historical diagnoses, lab results, drug purchases, and outstanding debt balances in a few clicks8.

### **Medicines, Batch Expiration, and Automated Demand Replenishment**

Inventory management is the operational centerpiece of BandaGo, engineered to eliminate drug stock-outs, prevent the sale of expired pharmaceuticals, and calculate optimal wholesale order quantities8. In the legacy OpenMRS stack (openmrs-module-openhmis.inventory), inventory relied on custom tables such as inv\_item, inv\_department, inv\_stockroom, inv\_stock\_operation, and inv\_recipient20. In the modern BandaGo architecture, medicines and clinical services are implemented on top of iDempiere's enterprise Material Management (M\_\*) engine14:

| Inventory Layer | Underlying iDempiere / BandaGo Table | Implementation & Reservation Mechanics |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **Medicine & Service Catalog** | M\_Product & M\_Product\_Category | Reserves M\_Product\_ID, M\_Product\_UU, Value (SKU/Code), Name (Generic/Brand Drug Name, Strength, Formulation), C\_UOM\_ID (Unit of Measure: tablet, vial, bottle, kit), and ProductType. Physical medicines and test kits use ProductType \= 'I' (Item, IsStocked \= 'Y'), whereas consultations and lab procedures use ProductType \= 'S' (Service, IsStocked \= 'N')13. |
| **Pricing & Margin Control** | M\_PriceList, M\_PriceList\_Version, M\_ProductPrice | Stores PriceStd (Standard POS Selling Price), PriceList, PriceLimit (minimum floor price to prevent unauthorized cashier discounting), and M\_Cost (purchase cost from wholesale suppliers)8. |
| **Batch, Lot & Expiration Dates** | M\_AttributeSet, M\_AttributeSetInstance (M\_ASI) | Every received batch of medicine generates a unique M\_AttributeSetInstance\_ID reserving Lot (Batch Number) and GuaranteeDate (Drug Expiration Date)13. |
| **Real-Time Stock Ledger** | M\_StorageOnHand, M\_Warehouse, M\_Locator | Tracks exact physical quantity (QtyOnHand) per M\_Product\_ID, per M\_Locator\_ID (Main Store vs. Dispensing Pharmacy Shelf), and per M\_AttributeSetInstance\_ID (specific expiration batch)8. |
| **Stock Movements & Audits** | M\_Transaction, M\_InOut, M\_Inventory, M\_Movement | Every stock change writes an immutable audit row to M\_Transaction: Vendor Receipts (M\_InOut V+), Patient POS Dispensing (M\_InOut C-), Internal Store-to-Pharmacy Transfers (M\_Movement), and Physical Stocktakes/Write-offs (M\_Inventory)8. |
| **Automated Demand Engine** | M\_Replenish & Custom PL/pgSQL Functions | Analyzes historical dispensing velocity (M\_Transaction / C\_OrderLine over time) to compute average daily consumption, lead-time buffer, and reorder quantities, firing automated restock notifications8. |

Under the hood, BandaGo's **Color-Coded Expiration Alerts** and **First-Expired, First-Out (FEFO)** dispensing rules are governed by joining M\_StorageOnHand with M\_AttributeSetInstance.GuaranteeDate13. When a pharmacist or cashier searches for a medicine at the POS, the GraphQL resolver queries M\_StorageOnHand ordered by GuaranteeDate ASC, flagging batches approaching expiration in yellow or red and blocking the dispensing of expired lots unless explicitly written off via an authorized M\_Inventory adjustment13.

### **Point-of-Sale, Cashier State Machine, and Financial Ledgers**

When a patient visit progresses to billing—or when a walk-in pharmacy customer purchases medication over the counter—BandaGo executes an atomic ERP Order-to-Cash workflow6. Comparing Banda Health's legacy OpenHMIS Cashier design with its current iDempiere POS implementation reveals how clinical billing rules were hardened into enterprise accounting ledgers.  
In the legacy openmrs-module-openhmis.cashier module, billing revolved around a single Bill entity (org.openmrs.module.openhmis.cashier.api.model.Bill) governed by a four-stage state machine12. A bill originated in the Pending state once it contained a patient and at least one line item and was saved via the Save Bill action, remaining freely editable without requiring an audit adjustment23. It transitioned to the Posted state automatically when partial or zero payment was processed, or manually via the Post Bill action, locking the bill for printing while leaving an outstanding balance23. Once total payments processed equaled or exceeded the bill total—incorporating configurable Floor, Mid, or Ceiling currency rounding via the Round To Nearest setting—the bill reached the Paid state23. Because posted and paid bills were immutable for auditing purposes, any subsequent modification or refund required transitioning the original bill to the Adjusted state, which generated a linked adjusting bill while locking the original record from further edits or printing23.  
In the modern **BandaGo iDempiere** architecture, this exact clinical cashier discipline is preserved at the UI layer but mapped under the hood to iDempiere's double-entry document engine (DocAction / DocStatus lifecycle: DR Drafted ![][image3] IP In Progress ![][image3] CO Completed ![][image3] RE Reversed/Voided)13:

| POS & Financial Document | Underlying iDempiere Table(s) | Under-the-Hood Transaction Mechanics |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **Visit Bill / POS Order** | C\_Order & C\_OrderLine | Created in DR (Draft/Pending) status as clinical notes, lab tests, and pharmacy prescriptions are added during the patient's visit. Reserves C\_BPartner\_ID, C\_DocTypeTarget\_ID (POS Order / Credit Order), M\_PriceList\_ID, GrandTotal, and line-level QtyOrdered, PriceActual, and M\_AttributeSetInstance\_ID6. |
| **Stock Dispensing** | M\_InOut & M\_InOutLine | Triggered automatically via base plugin model events upon POS Order completion (CO), immediately deducting dispensed drug quantities from M\_StorageOnHand13. |
| **Patient Invoice & Debt** | C\_Invoice & C\_InvoiceLine | Tracks the legal financial obligation. Reserves IsPaid ('Y'/'N'), GrandTotal, and OpenAmt (remaining unpaid debt). If a patient partially pays or leaves on credit, OpenAmt \> 0 persists on the patient's ledger, powering BandaGo's "who paid, who didn't pay" tracking and automated SMS debt reminders8. |
| **Tender & Payment Capture** | C\_Payment, C\_CashLine, C\_AllocationLine | Captures tender modes: Cash, Mobile Money (**M-Pesa**), Bank/Card, or Insurance/Government Schemes (**SHA** / NHIF). Links payments to invoices via C\_AllocationHdr and C\_AllocationLine to decrement OpenAmt6. |
| **Expense & Accounting Ledger** | Fact\_Acct, C\_ElementValue, C\_Charge | Every completed POS invoice, payment, vendor bill, and clinic expense posts balanced debit/credit entries to Fact\_Acct, generating real-time cash flow dashboards, income statements, payroll ledgers, and downloadable **KRA** statutory tax reports6. |

## **External Website Connectivity and API Endpoint Specifications**

For software architects and integration engineers seeking to connect an external website, patient portal, e-commerce storefront, or third-party health system to BandaGo POS, the platform exposes two primary programmatic API gateways—a modern **GraphQL API** and a native **iDempiere SOAP Web Service interface**—alongside specialized ecosystem connectors for national Health Information Exchanges (HIE) and mobile money13.  
![][image4]

### **Primary Integration Pathway: The Custom GraphQL API Plugin**

The primary, highest-performance integration surface for connecting external websites to BandaGo is the custom **GraphQL API plugin** (banda-health/idemp-plugins/graphql and graphql-feature)14. Unlike REST architectures that require multiple round-trip HTTP requests across disparate resource URLs, BandaGo's GraphQL server processes complex, nested client queries and mutations through a single unified HTTP POST endpoint, assembling relational data from across the iDempiere ERP layers into a single JSON graph response14. Furthermore, Banda Health maintains a dedicated TypeScript utility (banda-health/idempiere-log-parser) specifically engineered to parse iDempiere server logs for GraphQL statements to monitor query performance and API traffic7.  
Inspection of the graphql-test integration harness in idemp-plugins reveals the exact connection parameters and authentication mechanics required to establish a client session with the BandaGo server14:

| Connection Parameter / Feature | Technical Implementation & Usage |
| :---- | :---- |
| **IDEMPIERE\_ENDPOINT** | Base URL of the target BandaGo iDempiere instance exposing the OSGi HTTP/Jetty servlet container (e.g., https\://\<bandago-host\>/graphql or configured port endpoint)14. |
| **IDEMPIERE\_USER** | Authorized username (or email) corresponding to an active AD\_User record within the target clinic's AD\_Client tenant6. |
| **IDEMPIERE\_USER\_PASSWORD** | Password credential for the integration user account, subject to BandaGo's RBAC and password policies6. |
| **Dynamic Tenant Resolution** | Unlike legacy SOAP web services—which require hard-coding the target client inside XML request configurations—the GraphQL layer allows the client/tenant context (AD\_Client\_ID, AD\_Org\_ID, AD\_Role\_ID, M\_Warehouse\_ID) to be dynamically adjusted via environment configuration (.env) and authentication tokens14. |
| **Schema Generation & Testing** | GraphQL schema definitions and TypeScript test bindings are automatically generated during the Maven build of the graphql plugin (mvn verify), and validated via Jest (npm test \-- \--run inside graphql-test/testing)14. |

When an external website connects to the GraphQL endpoint, it interacts with BandaGo's business domain through strongly-typed **Queries** (read operations) and **Mutations** (write/transactional operations) mapped to the underlying base plugin models14. Based on BandaGo's functional modules and Jest test suite (such as visitReceiptReport.test.ts), the GraphQL schema exposes the following core functional domains for external integration6:

| Functional Domain | GraphQL Operation Type | Target ERP / BandaGo Entities | External Website Integration Use Cases |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **Authentication & Context** | Mutation (login / changeRole) | AD\_User, AD\_Session, AD\_Client, AD\_Org, AD\_Role | Authenticating an external web portal, acquiring a bearer/session token, and selecting the clinic branch (AD\_Org\_ID) and RBAC role6. |
| **Patient & Customer Directory** | Query & Mutation | C\_BPartner (IsCustomer='Y'), C\_BPartner\_Location | Searching patients by phone/name/national ID, registering new patients from an online booking website, or checking a customer's unpaid debt balance (TotalOpenBalance)8. |
| **Patient Visits & Queues** | Query & Mutation | Custom Visit Entity (BH\_Visit), Clinical Notes, Lab Orders | Scheduling appointments from an external website, pushing a newly arrived patient into the clinic's live waiting queue, or retrieving visit history6. |
| **Medicine Catalog & Live Stock** | Query & Mutation | M\_Product, M\_ProductPrice, M\_StorageOnHand, M\_ASI | Querying real-time pharmacy stock levels (QtyOnHand), unit prices (PriceStd), and batch expiration dates (GuaranteeDate) for an online pharmacy storefront or B2B wholesale supplier portal8. |
| **POS Billing & Payments** | Mutation | C\_Order, C\_OrderLine, C\_Invoice, C\_Payment | Submitting an external e-commerce pharmacy order into the POS queue, posting an M-Pesa payment callback against an open patient bill, or generating a receipt6. |
| **Reports & Receipts** | Query | JasperReports Engine (visitReceiptReport, MOH705, Financial Ledgers) | Fetching compiled PDF/HTML visit receipts, patient transaction statements, or statutory summary reports8. |

### **Secondary Integration Pathway: Native iDempiere SOAP Web Services**

In addition to the custom GraphQL plugin, BandaGo retains and actively tests **iDempiere's native SOAP Web Services** (./dev.sh test graphql runs both SOAP and Jest test suites, and the repository explicitly notes that *"the SOAP webservices are configured as this client"*)14. Under the hood, iDempiere's web service container (/ADInterface/services/ModelADService and /ADInterface/services/compositeInterface) is governed by the WS\_WebService, WS\_WebServiceType, WS\_WebService\_Para, and WS\_WebServiceFieldInput tables in PostgreSQL. External enterprise systems or ERP connectors can communicate with BandaGo via XML SOAP envelopes over HTTPS using standard model and document operations:

| SOAP Web Service Operation | Target Interface Endpoint | Transactional Behavior in BandaGo |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **queryData / readData** | /ADInterface/services/ModelADService | Retrieves rows from any permitted table (e.g., C\_BPartner, M\_Product, C\_Invoice) using SQL-like filter criteria14. |
| **createData / updateData / createUpdateData** | /ADInterface/services/ModelADService | Inserts or updates records (such as syncing a master drug catalog or creating a customer record) while firing all BandaGo base plugin Model Events and Callouts14. |
| **setDocAction** | /ADInterface/services/ModelADService | Transitions a transactional document (such as a C\_Order POS bill or M\_InOut stock receipt) from DR (Draft) to CO (Completed), triggering inventory deduction and General Ledger posting14. |
| **runProcess** | /ADInterface/services/ModelADService | Executes a server-side SvrProcess or JasperReport by its AD\_Process\_ID14. |
| **compositeOperation** | /ADInterface/services/compositeInterface | Bundles multiple operations (e.g., create C\_BPartner \+ create C\_Order \+ create C\_OrderLine \+ setDocAction Complete \+ create C\_Payment) inside a single atomic database transaction so that if any step fails, the entire POS checkout rolls back cleanly14. |

Every SOAP request requires an \<ADLoginRequest\> block containing \<user\>, \<pass\>, \<ClientID\>, \<RoleID\>, \<OrgID\>, \<WarehouseID\>, and \<stage\>. Because SOAP web service types in iDempiere must be explicitly configured per tenant (AD\_Client\_ID) and granted role permissions in WS\_WebServiceTypeAccess, the GraphQL endpoint remains far more flexible for multi-clinic web integrations14.

### **Ecosystem Gateways: HIE, SHA, M-Pesa, and Network Security Governance**

Beyond general-purpose GraphQL and SOAP interfaces, BandaGo's architecture incorporates specialized external integration gateways tailored to the Kenyan and East African healthcare regulatory landscape, with external endpoints simulated during CI testing via the external-mocks directory in idemp-plugins13. Specifically, BandaGo holds official Level 2 and Level 3A **Kenya Digital Health Agency (DHA)** certification and full **Health Information Exchange (HIE)** integration13. This connectivity enables BandaGo to exchange standardized patient, clinical (ICD-11), and claim payloads with the national health grid and validate or submit reimbursement claims directly to the **Social Health Authority (SHA)**, eliminating claim rejections through mandatory field validation13. On the financial and patient communication front, subscription billing and clinic cash flows integrate with Safaricom's **M-Pesa** ecosystem—where Banda Health processes subscription payments via M-Pesa Paybill 600100, Account 0100002964947, and clinics record M-Pesa patient tenders at the POS—while an outbound **Automated SMS Gateway** dispatches appointment follow-ups, targeted clinic marketing campaigns, and unpaid debt reminders directly from C\_BPartner phone records6.  
Architects planning to connect an external website to a hosted BandaGo cloud instance must account for strict operational and legal boundaries. At the infrastructure layer, Banda Health enforces strict ingress and egress firewall rules on its production servers, restricting direct network access and continuously monitoring traffic in consultation with US-based data security experts15. Furthermore, under the BandaGo Service Level Agreement (SLA) and Terms of Service, each clinic acts as the Data Controller responsible for managing and authorizing its AD\_User accounts, while unauthorized scraping, reproduction, or unapproved third-party access to the platform is contractually prohibited6. Consequently, connecting an external website to BandaGo in production requires one of two deployment pathways: an organization must either self-host the open-source stack by deploying banda-health/idempiere-docker and compiling banda-health/idemp-plugins onto a self-managed cloud environment where the integrator controls the IDEMPIERE\_ENDPOINT firewall and PostgreSQL database7, or coordinate directly with Banda Health (info@bandahealth.org) and the target clinic owner for authorized cloud whitelisting, provisioning a dedicated integration AD\_User and AD\_Role, whitelisting the external website's IP or CORS origin at the firewall, and obtaining the production IDEMPIERE\_ENDPOINT GraphQL URL6.

## **Architectural Synthesis and Integration Recommendations**

BandaGo represents a highly pragmatic, domain-hardened evolution in global health informatics. By migrating away from fragile OpenMRS clinical add-on modules (openmrs-module-openhmis.\*) and rebuilding its stack on **iDempiere ERP**, **PostgreSQL (with PL/pgSQL)**, **OSGi plugins (base and graphql)**, and **ReactJS/TypeScript**, Banda Health solved the dual challenge of clinical documentation and small-business financial survival7. Under the hood, every patient is an ERP Business Partner (C\_BPartner), every medicine batch is an attribute-tracked stock instance (M\_Product \+ M\_AttributeSetInstance \+ M\_StorageOnHand), and every outpatient visit seamlessly compiles clinical notes, ICD-11 diagnoses, lab panels, and pharmacy prescriptions into double-entry POS orders (C\_Order), invoices (C\_Invoice), payments (C\_Payment), and General Ledger postings (Fact\_Acct)6.  
For engineering teams designing external website integrations with BandaGo POS, the optimal architectural strategy begins by targeting the custom **GraphQL Plugin (graphql)** over legacy SOAP web services. External web applications should integrate exclusively via the GraphQL endpoint configured through IDEMPIERE\_ENDPOINT, IDEMPIERE\_USER, and IDEMPIERE\_USER\_PASSWORD14. Unlike iDempiere's native SOAP interface, which binds requests to static client definitions and requires verbose XML payloads, the GraphQL layer supports dynamic multi-tenant context resolution, UUID-based entity lookups, and exact field projection in a single HTTPS round-trip14.  
Prior to attempting production connectivity, integration engineers should bootstrap a local contract-testing sandbox using Banda Health's containerized tooling. By cloning banda-health/idemp-plugins, executing mvn verify and ./dev.sh test (or docker compose \-f docker-compose.dev.yml up \--build), and inspecting the auto-generated GraphQL schema and Jest integration tests inside graphql-test/testing, developers can obtain the exact, up-to-date GraphQL query and mutation signatures for patient registration, inventory queries, and visit receipt generation without risking production data integrity14.  
Finally, any external integration must strictly preserve ERP document lifecycle integrity by never bypassing the graphql or base plugin layers to write directly to PostgreSQL tables. Because BandaGo relies on OSGi Model Events, Column Callouts, and PL/pgSQL functions to synchronize stock levels (M\_StorageOnHand), compute medicine demand forecasts, enforce FEFO expiration locks, and post balanced accounting entries (Fact\_Acct), all external website transactions must flow through the GraphQL mutation resolvers or SOAP ModelADService endpoints so that BandaGo's internal business logic and data-integrity-alerter checks remain fully intact7.
